Skytruth Analysis
SEVERAL EMISSIONS PERIODS OCCURRED WHICH MAY HAVE EXCEEDED THE REPORTABLE QUANTITY FOR SULFUR DIOXIDE (SO2) DURING START-UPS AT THIS NEW FACILITY. THE CONTINUOUS EMISSIONS MONITORING SYSTEM IN PLACE FOR SO2 EMISSIONS HAS NOT YET BEEN CERTIFIED AND WORK IS ON-GOING TO RESOLVE POTENTIAL DATA QUALITY ISSUES. THE EXCESS SO2 EMISSIONS OCCURRED DURING START-UPS IN OCT. DUE TO AN ISSUE WITH PRE-HEATER EXPANSION JOINTS AND IN DEC. DUE TO POOR QUALITY OF REFINERY GAS FEEDS TO THE PLANT. THESE ISSUES HAVE BEEN ADDRESSED. APPROXIMATE TIMES AND DURATIONS FOR RELEASES OF SO2 THAT WERE IN EXCESS OF THE REPORTABLE QUANTITY, WHICH IS 500 LBS. PER LISTING IN 40 CFR 355, APPENDIX A, LIST OF EXTREMELY HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES, AND ESTIMATED QUANTITIES HAVE BEEN INCLUDED IN THE TABLE BELOW: DATE START, TIME START, DATE END, TIME END, QUANTITY SO2, DURATION 10/18/05, 3:00, 10/19/05, 3:00, 1118 LBS., 24 HOURS (RESENDING AS SEPARATE REPORTS PER NRC REQUEST. THE EXCESS SO2 EMISSIONS OCCURRED DURING START-UPS IN OCT. DUE TO AN ISSUE WITH PRE-HEATER EXPANSION JOINTS AND IN DEC. DUE TO POOR QUALITY OF REFINERY GAS FEEDS TO THE PLANT. THESE ISSUES HAVE BEEN ADDRESSED. APPROXIMATE TIMES AND DURATIONS FOR RELEASES OF SO2 THAT WERE IN EXCESS OF THE REPORTABLE QUANTITY, WHICH IS 500 LBS. THE PIPELINE IS A SUB-SEA TRANSFER PIPELINE THAT EXPERIENCED A PRESSURE DIFFERENTIAL DROP. MOST LIKELY CAUSE IS PIPE CORROSION. THE LINE HAS BEEN SHUT-IN AND IS CONFIRMED SECURED AT EACH END, BUT 67 MILES OF PIPELINE REMAIN BETWEEN ISOLATION VALVES. OVERFLIGHTS HAVE VERIFIED DARK OILY SURFACE SHEEN OVER THE PRESUMED RUPTURE LOCATION.

Medium Affected: WATER

Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 0.33 feet by 0.33 feet (area 0.11 sq. ft.)
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0 gallons
WHILE WALKING ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER’S BANK (ALONG THE REVETMENT) ON JANUARY 20, 2011, SMALL SHEEN CIRCLES WERE OBSERVED ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON-AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRED ON NOVEMBER 10, 2010, AND WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC UNDER INCIDENT REPORT # 959615 AND LDEQ SPOC SYSTEM INCIDENT REPORT # GT01 8451. THIS AREA IS CURRENTLY BEING INVESTIGATED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE LDEQ (AI NO. 1708).

CALLER STATES THAT IT IS UNKNOWN IF THERE WERE ANY RELEASES FROM THE PASSENGER TRUCKS INVOLVED IN THIS INCIDENT.

properties.title: NRC Report: Sodium Hydroxide (In Black Liquor Sludge) near Groveton, NH
properties.summary: Incident Type: STORAGE TANK - NRC Report ID: 861203 - Medium Affected: OTHER - Suspected Responsible Party: ALLIED RECYCLING, INC.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 861203
Incident Time: 2008-01-27 05:00:00
Nearest City: Groveton, NH
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: SODIUM HYDROXIDE (IN BLACK LIQUOR SLUDGE)
Medium Affected: OTHER
Suspected Responsible Party: ALLIED RECYCLING, INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 100 gallons
CATERPILLAR IS SENIOR SECURED CREDITOR OF GROVETON PAPER BOARD, BANKRUPT OWNER OF PROPERTY ON WHICH SPILL OCCURRED. CATERPILLAR, AS SECURED CREDITOR, SOLD A TANK TO SUSPECTED RESPONSIBLE PARTY, ALLIED RECYCLING, INC. TANK IS LOCATED INSIDE AN INDUSTRIAL BUILDING. ALLIED PURCHASED AND BEGAN DEMOLISHING TANK FOR SCRAP. DURING TANK DEMOLITION, SLUDGE IN TANK WAS RELEASED ONTO BUILDING FLOOR. SLUDGE IS BELIEVED TO BE BLACK LIQUOR, AQUEOUS SOLUTION TYPICALLY COMPOSED OF LIGNIN RESIDUES, HEMICELLULOSE, SODIUM SULFIDE, AND SODIUM HYDROXIDE. MATERIAL IS TYPICALLY HIGH PH DUE TO PRESENCE OF SODIUM HYDROXIDE. FIELD TESTING INDICATED PH IN RANGE OF 10-12. WATER FROM PARTIALLY DEMOLISHED ROOF DRAIN ENTERED SPILL ROOM, MIXED WITH SLUDGE, AND FLOWED OUT OF ROOM INTO NEARBY DRAINAGE SYSTEM. FROM DRAINAGE SYSTEM, DISCHARGED INTO INDUSTRIAL WASTE WATER TREATMENT PLANT OPERATED BY WAUSAU PAPER. WAUSAU DETECTED HIGHER THAN NORMAL PH IN WASTE WATER IN PRIMARY CLARIFIER AND NOTIFIED CATERPILLAR'S AGENT OF APPARENT RELEASE. IT'S NATURE OF THE MATERIAL IS NOT FULLY KNOWN AT THIS POINT (LABORATORY SAMPLES COLLECTED FOR ANALYSIS); MASS OF MATERIAL RELEASED IS NOT KNOWN. HOWEVER, IT IS POSSIBLE THAT MASS O MATERIAL RELEASED EXCEEDED THE RQ FOR NAOH. WAUSAU REPORTED THAT HIGH PH WATER WAS TREATED AND DID NOT ENTER WATERS RECEIVING TREATMENT PLANT DISCHARGE.

***WEB REPORT*** THE PURPOSE OF THIS CORRESPONDENCE IS TO UPDATE THE CERCLA 103(F)(2) CONTINUOUS RELEASE REPORT FOR THIS FACILITY, ORIGINALLY REPORTED UNDER CR-ERNS NUMBER 40770. IN CONJUNCTION WITH REVIEWING THE 2011 TRI REPORT AND MILL-WIDE EMISSIONS INVENTORY, WE HAVE REVIEWED THE PREVIOUSLY SUBMITTED CONTINUOUS RELEASE DATA AND PROVIDE THE ENCLOSED UPDATED INFORMATION. AS REQUIRED UNDER 40 CFR 302.8(G)(2), NOTIFICATION MUST BE GIVEN IF THERE IS A CHANGE IN A RELEASE SUCH THAT THE QUANTITY OF THE RELEASE EXCEEDS THE UPPER BOUND OF THE PREVIOUSLY REPORTED NORMAL RANGE, RESULTING IN A STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT INCREASE IN THE RELEASE. IN COMPLIANCE WITH THIS REGULATION, WE ARE REPORTING THAT THE UPPER BOUND OF THE REPORTED NORMAL RANGE FOR ACROLEIN HAS CHANGED FROM 11 LBS/DAY TO 15 LBS/DAY. THE CHANGE FOR ACROLEIN RESULTED FROM THE MILL USING UPDATED EMISSIONS FACTORS FROM NCASI TB 973 TABLES 4.1, 4.11, 4.13, 4.14, 4.15, 4.16, 4.17, 4.18, 4.19, 4.20, 4.21, 4.23, 4.25, 4.28, 4.30, 4.31, 4.33, 4.32, 4.35, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.9, 4.10, 5.1, 5.2, 6.3, 7.1, 10.2, 10.5, 10.6, AND 10.8 AND FROM AP-42 TABLES 1.1-14 AND 3.1-3.
